title: Third and commonest opinion: only conjectural hope-certainty joined with some fear
source_text: XXI. Igitur in Ecclesia Romana plurimum obtinet, & longe communior est tertia quaedam sententia, quae non tantum fidelibus negat certitudinem fidei circa propriam justitiam, sed etiam moralem illam certitudinem quae excludit omnem formidinem & timorem deceptionis, & nisi adsit quaedam specialis revelatio, locum hic habere vult eam solum certitudinem quam conjecturalem vocant, & certitudinem spei, seu fiduciae, quae cum quadam formidine & timore conjuncta est, sed tamen ex animo expellit dubitationem & fluctuationem, per quam quis non auderet judicare se Deo acceptum, & de peccatorum suorum remissione confidere, & proinde sufficit ad animum tranquillandum, & pacem conscientiae in fidelibus & justis gignendam.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore in the Roman Church a certain third opinion most obtains, and is by far the more common, which not only denies to the faithful the certainty of faith concerning their own righteousness, but also that moral certainty which excludes every fear and dread of deception; and unless some special revelation is present, it wants to have place here only that certainty which they call conjectural, and the certainty of hope or trust, which is joined with a certain fear and dread, yet nevertheless drives from the mind doubt and fluctuation by which someone would not dare judge himself accepted by God and trust concerning the remission of his sins, and therefore suffices to quiet the mind and to beget peace of conscience in the faithful and just.
pass_b_english: The common Roman third view allows only conjectural hope-certainty of one’s justification.
Some fear remains, yet fluctuating doubt is expelled enough for peace of conscience—absent special revelation.
